messages:
viv: RFC follow-up: propose a lightweight 'delegation shim' for service-to-service auth. Goal: avoid creating per-route API keys while keeping least privilege. Short sketch below.

omar: quick overview pls — tradeoffs?

viv: sketch: broker mints ephemeral delegated tokens (<=4m). caller holds long-lived key only for minting; runtime only sees ephemeral token + X-Actor header which encodes actor:project:role. runtime validates signature, checks policy cache, enforces route allowlist.

jin: migration concern: legacy integrations still call with long-lived keys. plan?

viv: broker will issue mapped ephemeral tokens on first seen legacy call (shadow mode). console + SDK provide exchange flow. after canary, we route enforcement to ephemeral-only for public routes.

auth-bot: task created: AUTH-512 implement jwks cache and edge policy cache :white_check_mark:

omar: perf: local jwks verification + cache TTL 20s, policy cache TTL 10s. measure in perf lab.

jin: security: add X-Actor-Chain to preserve origin -> broker -> actor trail for auditing and billing. revoke via broker revoke endpoint.

oviv: next: I'll write RFC addendum with token format, header examples, JWKS rotation, and migration timeline. ping infra/devex for SDK + console work.
